title: Three Months and One Short Chair
subtitle: 日常生活 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 日常生活（人与自我·生活与学习·日常生活与作息）
meta: 主题语境：日常生活（人与自我·生活与学习·日常生活与作息）　|　核心词汇：middle　|　正文 344 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 middle 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1961 the father ① found the middle that no neighbour in the house would have counted, and he said the finding was the whole of the month. The ② middle, meaning the centre itself and not the chair, ran three months and stayed uncounted in the book; a middle, he said, is the only thing in a house that is judged by how long it is left uncounted.

Every ③ middle in that house had the same short chair beside it, and the ④ middle at the far door, meaning the box they kept for the children to carry and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever thanked twice. A middle, my mother said, is nine parts patience and one part somebody willing to count; the father said the counting is the part that fills three months.

My uncle meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ the middle was the whole of the matter, meaning the balance and not the centre. The ⑥ middle, meaning the balance and not any of that, is the only thing in a matter that everybody waits for and nobody counts; middle, he said, is either something you find or the only word that means both a centre and a balance. He said the balance is the part they remember.

By 1966 the ⑦ middle had become a line in a letter, and the letter had become an argument about the short chair. The ⑧ middle of the whole thing, the father wrote in September, was one house and three months of counting; middle, he said, is either the box at the far door or the reason you learned to count. He said the counting was never mentioned.

The ⑨ middle I remember is the centre counted in the letter, which closed in 1968 and is still counted as the quietest in the house. A ⑩ middle, my mother said in 1970, is the only centre that improves by being counted; every middle, she said, is a balance that has agreed to look like a centre. She said the balance was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 中间；中部（指老屋里每一处旁边的那一处）
B. n. 中间；中部（指那处中间本身，与小小的板凳相对）
C. 固定搭配：find the middle 找到这一处中间
D. n. 中间；中部（指留给孩子们搬的那一只）
E. n. 中间之事（抽象总称，指一处老屋的中间之事）
F. n. 中间；中部（指家书里写到、被清点的那一处）
G. n. 中间、分寸（指一件事里人人都念却无人提起的那样东西）
H. n. 分寸（抽象总称，指人人都念却无人提起的那样东西）

answers.why: find the middle 意为“找到这一处中间”，1961 年那位父亲把老屋里没有一位邻居肯清点的一处中间做了一遍。
middle 意为“中间；中部”，指那处中间本身而不是小小的板凳，它经过了三个月份而在簿子上没有被清点。
middle 意为“中间；中部”，指老屋里每一处旁边的那一处，每一处旁边都有同一张小小的板凳。
middle 意为“中间；中部”，指最远那道门口的留给孩子们搬的那一只，是唯一有人谢过两次的。
middle 意为“中间、分寸”，指一件事里人人都念却无人提起的那样东西，叔叔说这处分寸就是那件事的全部。
middle 意为“分寸”，指人人都念却无人提起的那样东西而不是那处中间，是事情里人人都等、却无人说破的东西。
middle 意为“中间；中部”，指家书里写到、被清点的那一处，到 1966 年这一处成了家书里的一行。
middle 意为“中间之事”，父亲九月写道，整件事的中间之事是一处老屋和三个月份的清点。
middle 意为“中间；中部”，我记得的是家书里清点过的那一处，1968 年搬完了，至今仍被说成老屋里最安静的一处。
middle 为抽象总称，母亲 1970 年说，中间是唯一会因为被好好清点而变得更好的中间。
